pr.rehberAlt: The way of the cards, the myths and the reading
hk.ceviri: The translation of this text will be added after legal review. The Turkish original is shown below.
rh.giris: In ancient times people looked to the sky, the earth and the dream, and poured what they saw into stories. Logos gathers six great rivers of those stories at a single table. Here the cards do not command your future; they hold up a mirror and help you read your path in your own words.
rh.1.m: In ancient Greek, logos meant word, meaning, and the order that holds the cosmos together. For Heraclitus everything flows, yet within the flow there is a measure. These cards were woven to seek that measure: to put into words the pattern hidden in days that seem scattered.
rh.2.m: The thirty-six cards are divided into six houses, and each house is the gate of a mythology. Aetherion takes the order of the heavens from the Aztec sun. Prometheion carries the fire of humankind from the Greek myths. Ragnarion tells of ruin and rebirth from the Norse sagas. Alcherion listens to the memory of the land, inspired by Aboriginal Dreaming traditions. Duation teaches the passage through darkness from the Egyptian underworld. Samsarion weaves the wheel of time with the red thread of fate from East Asia.
rh.3.m: Your six chosen cards take six places in turn. Root tells where this moment comes from. Now shows the energy you are in. Trial opens the lesson before you. Ally calls the power that supports you. Path whispers what is opening soon. Fate points to where the journey arrives. The cards lie face down; it is intuition, not the eye, that chooses.
rh.4.m: As you lay each card you give it a stance. An upright card is energy that has risen; it calls to movement, word and action. A sideways card is not asleep but ripening; it turns inward, waits and steeps. No card is bad or reversed; each is simply the voice of another time.
rh.5.m: In many traditions the raven and the crow carry news between two worlds. Odin's ravens Huginn and Muninn carry thought and memory; Apollo's crow carries prophecy. The house that shines strongest in your reading sends you its own crow, and its saying is the key sentence of your reading.
rh.6.m: Each card is bound to a real mythological figure and carries the lesson told of that figure for centuries. The card's own story is an original tale of Logos; myth and story stand side by side and never blur. In the card library you can read each card's source and lesson.
rh.7.m: Your chosen cards are interpreted together with your sign, your intention and your question. The interpretation is written by AI, staying true to the meanings of the cards and the lessons of the myths. A short reading gives the essence. A full reading builds the bridges between the cards. A deep reading weaves the six cards into a single journey from Root to Fate.
rh.8.m: You can also open the cards for a friend. When you begin a reading, choose A guest and enter their date of birth. The reading counts towards your plan and is kept in your history under their name.
rh.9.m: Do not ask the cards the same question again and again; the answer to a question ripens with time. Use the reading as a compass, not a map. The last step is always yours to take.
